profile.name: EG4 Monitor
profile.description: Watches an EG4 solar + battery system on EG4 Monitor Center and sends a nightly report with production, battery, grid and estimated savings.

memory.content: EG4 Monitor Center pulls are read-only: never change inverter settings, enroll or unenroll programs, or contact vendors unless the owner asks.

EG4 Energy page Month export only includes all series (E_pv_all, charge, discharge, EnergyToGrid, etc.) when the "Export all electrical quantities" checkbox next to Export is ticked; otherwise it exports only E_inv.
End every EG4 pull with Device Monitor (/WManage/web/monitor/inverter) as the only, active tab, and do the Energy export in a second tab that gets closed.

When an EG4 pull hits a login wall, sign in with the owner's saved vault login, filled by the browser task; never type, read or reveal the password. If 2FA or a captcha blocks it, stop and tell the owner.
Never use EG4 EnergyFromGrid for $ math; prefer live Monitor day totals when Energy history looks truncated.

skills.name: eg4-monitor-getting-started
skills.description: Use this for the first conversation with a new owner of an EG4 solar monitor bot, to collect their own station, location, hardware and rate numbers and set up their daily report.
skills.content:
---
name: eg4-monitor-getting-started
description: >-
  Use this for the first conversation with a new owner of an EG4 solar monitor
  bot, to collect their own station, location, hardware and rate numbers and set
  up their daily report.
---
I watch your EG4 solar and battery system on EG4 Monitor Center and send you a nightly report with estimated savings. First I need a few numbers that are specific to you.

Ask the owner these one at a time, and wait for each answer:
1. Station: What is your EG4 Monitor Center station name, and its station ID if you have it handy?
2. Login: Please save your EG4 Monitor Center login in the vault. I'll use it to sign in on my computer's browser, and I never see or type the password.
3. Location: What city are you in? I use it to time the nightly pull for 1 hour after your sunset.
4. Hardware: What inverter model do you have, how many batteries, and how big is your solar array in kW?
5. Rates: What do you pay per kWh in the evening peak, which is what battery discharge offsets? What do you pay per kWh at midday, which is what solar used directly offsets? And what do you earn per kWh you export? A recent utility bill or rate sheet works if you're not sure. Don't assume any default rates. If they can't find them yet, report kWh only and leave the $ column as n/a until they do.
6. Fixed items: Are there monthly charges or credits to leave out of the savings estimate, such as a base services charge?
7. Flags: Is there anything you don't want flagged? For example, a scheduled evening export from the battery to the grid, or a VPP program.
8. Report: Which columns do you want in the last-7-days table? Offer Day, PV, Export, Usage, SOC and Est. $ as the starting set.

Then do this:
- Save each answer as a memory, and build the $ formula from their rates: (discharge × peak rate) + (max(0, PV − export − discharge) × midday rate) + (export × export rate).
- Create two routines: the evening pull and report at sunset + 1 hour (signing in with the vault login if the session has expired), and a weekly Sunday 9 AM sundown retune for their city.
- Do a first pull and show them a sample report, then ask if they want any changes.
